This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 7 September 1950 on the endorsement by the Chemical Division Council of the draft finalized on 8 June 1950 by the Paints and Allied Products It is based largely on Sectional Committee. the interim co-ordinated draft produced with the assistance of the representatives of manufacturers and of various departments and authorities of the Government of India, by the Co-ordinating Subcommittee of the No. 5 Standing Committee on Specifications for Paints and Allied Stores of the General Head1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of test for the material commercially known as Ready Mixed Paint, Brushing, Petrol Resisting, Stoving, for Interior Painting of Tanks and Containers, Red Oxide ( colour unspecified ). The material is used for the interior protection of petrol tanks and containers and issuch that on stoving, it gives a film which is petrol resisting and does not increase " gumming " of petrol. 1.2 This standard is intended chiefly to cover the technical provisions relating to the purchase of the material, but it does not include all the necessary provisions of a contract. 2. TERMINOLOGY .

samples of the material as prescribed under 3 of

4. REQUIREMENTS 4.1 Composition - The material shall be of such a composition as to satisfy the requirements of this standard. 4.2 Freedom from Copper - The material shall be free from copper and compounds of copper. 4.3 Resistance to Fuel for Aeroengines and Effect on Fuel 4.3.1 When the test drum treated with the material is tested as described in Appendix A, the paint film shall show no surface defects. 4.3.2 The fuel for aerocngines, stored as described in Appendix A and tested as dcscribed in Appendix B, shall not show an incrcasc in existent gum hy more tllan 10 mg per 100 ml of fuel. 4.4 The material shall also conform requirements in Table I. to th,:

2.1 For the purposes of this standard, the delinitions given under 2 of IS : 101-1950 shall apply. 3. SAMPLE 3.1 The vendor shall submit a tender sample packed in three different containers, each containing not less than 500 g of the material. 3.2 The purchaser may select, as approved sample, the sample submitted by the vendor, or any other agreed sample. References to the relevant clauses of that standard are given in column (4) in Table I. 5.2 The tests marked with an asterisk shall be carried out on stoved films after keeping for 24 hours at room temperature. 5.2.1 Unless otherwise agreed between the purchaser and the vendor, the stoving temperature and time shall be 150�C and 30 minutes for dark colours, and 93�C and 1 hour for pale and light colours.

APPENDIX A ( Clause 4.3.1 )
DETERMINATION A-l. PREPARATION NER OF RESISTANCE OF THE TO AEROENGINE FUEL AND EFFECT ON FUEL CONTAIA-2. PROCEDURE A-2.1 Store 200 ml of fuel for aeroengines in the container and keep the container at a temperature between 21" and 38�C. After one month, examine the paint film for blistering, cracking or any other surface defect.

A-l.1 Flush with the paint a cylindrical, pickled, cold-rolled, close annealed, mild steel plate contnincr, 2.5 in ( or 60 mm ) in diameter and 3 in ( or 73 mm ) high, provided with a well fitting lid and allow the excess to drain off. Stove dry the dark colours at 150�C and light and pale colours at 93�C. Allow the container to dry for a period of seven days at room temperature. 3

A-2.1.1 Reserve the aeroengine as described in Appendix B.

APPENDIX ( Clause 4.3.2 )
DETERMINATION

B

OF THE EXISTENT GUM B-2.1.1 For shall be used.
referee tests a Bunsen flame

B-l. APPARATUS El.1
The following apparatus is required: of about 250 Flask -round-bottomed, ml total capacity with ground joint. Alternatively, a distillation flask may be used. Distillation head to fit the tlask. with a ground joint

4

b)
4

Condenser - Liebig type, fitted with a bent end which does not hold up liquid when assembled. Graduated receiver of 100 ml capacity. in shape, without lip, 66 f 2 mm in external diameter, and 18 f 3 g in weight.

4

Dishes -hemispherical e>

B-2.2 Disconnect the flask from the distillation head and pour the contents into one of the dishes which has been heated previously in steam oven, cooled in dust-free atmosphere for 15 to 20 minutes and weighed to an accuracy of & 0 2 mg on a balance shielded from direct sunlight. Allow the flask to drain into the dish in an inverted vertical position for 15 seconds. Place the dish at once on a vigorously boiling water bath and allow it to remain supported in a hole having a diameter of 64 & 1 mm and protected from dust, for one and a half hours. B-2.2.1 In the case of fuels distilling less than 50 percent at 100�C and less than 95 percent at 145'C, continue the evaporation on the water bath, if necessary, for a longer period than one and a half hours, and until evaporation is complete. B-2.3 After evaporating on the water bath transfer the dish to a water or steam oven and allow it to remain at a temperature of 100" & 2�C for one hour. Allow the dish to cool for 15 to 20 minutes in a dust-free atmosphere and weigh to an accuracy of f 0.2 mg. B-2.4 Repeat the test with aeroengine fuel without storing it in the prepared container and treat the result as a blank. B-3. CALCULATION B-3.1 Express the residue on evaporation as milligrams of residue per 100 ml of the fuel. B-3.2 The prescribed lirpit fur increase in existent gum shall be taken as not having been exceeded if the difference in weight, if any, of the residue on evaporation in the test and the blank is not more than 10 mg per 100 ml of the fuel,

B-l.? The

flask, distillation head, receiver, condenser and dishes shall be made entirely of Pyrex or Hysil or Monax or Geraote-20 glass. B-2. PROCEDURE

B-2.1 Measure 100 ml of the aeroengine fuel, stored as described in Appendix A, into the flask and connect it to the distillation head. Place the flask on an asbestos sheet, 150 mm in diameter and having a central hole 40 mm in diameter. Pass the delivery end of the condenser through a two-hole cork inserted in the 100 ml graduated receiver. Provide the cork with another tube through which the gases and uncondensed vapours evolved during the distillation can be led away from any source of ignition. Bring the contents of the flask cautiously to boiling over a boiling water bath or a hot plate or a Bunsen flame, avoiding any sudden evolution of vapour. Distil at the rate of 4 to 5 ml per minute or about two drops per second until 75 ml of distillate are collected in the graduated receiver.
